why: A real NEAR candidate whose formal/ tree is byte-identical to the reference reexec-witness, so its certificate is correct about the model ReexecWitness.Model.verifier and would pass every formal gate. The shipped out/verify, however, is a different (Rust) binary that also accepts any claim whose proof starts with EVIL. Under verify_route = native-lean only the judge's own compilation of formal.verifier_model may run as the verifier; a candidate-shipped verifier whose digest differs from that build must fail ARTIFACT_BINDING. Admitting it, or running the shipped binary as the verifier, would let a forged claim through.
notes: NEAR-specific: submit against the near-transfer-receipt-v1 challenge. Verified locally: out/verify accepts a forged claim (refunds fields altered) with proof bytes 'EVIL'; the reference verifier rejects it. The formal certificate (types for any binary digest because the native edge is trusted) still elaborates, so FORMAL_* gates may PASS; the kill must come from binding the built artifact to the judge build (runners/formal-checker native.rs candidate_binary_digest).
